signalling-pathway.short: A chain of molecules inside a cell that passes a message along, each one switching on the next, until something changes, such as which genes are read.

gene-expression.short: Reading a gene to make its product: first a copy called mRNA, then the protein built from that copy. Training changes which genes are read, and how much.

mrna.short: Messenger RNA: a short-lived working copy of one gene, which the cell uses as the recipe to build a protein. More mRNA usually means more of that protein is being made.

camk.short: Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase: an enzyme switched on when calcium (Ca²⁺) rises inside a muscle fibre with each contraction. It passes the 'muscle is working' message on.

ampk.short: AMP-activated protein kinase: the cell's fuel gauge. It switches on when ATP runs low and AMP builds up, and turns on processes that make more ATP.

p38-mapk.short: A stress-sensing enzyme (one of the mitogen-activated protein kinases). It is switched on by stresses such as reactive oxygen species and by calcium signals, and helps switch on PGC-1α.

pgc-1a.short: A protein that helps switch on many genes at once, especially those for building mitochondria. Often called the master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis.

mitochondrial-biogenesis.short: The building of new mitochondria, and the growth of existing ones, inside muscle fibres: the muscle's response to the stress of training.

mtdna.short: The small set of genes inside each mitochondrion, separate from the cell's main DNA. Sometimes used as a marker of how many mitochondria there are, though a poor one.

respirometry.short: Measuring how fast a sample uses oxygen. Here: small bundles of muscle fibres from a biopsy are fed fuels in a sealed chamber to measure their mitochondria's oxygen use.

sprint-interval-training.short: Intervals of all-out sprints, usually 30 s or shorter, harder than the power that draws out VO₂max, each followed by a long easy recovery of a few minutes.

eccentric-hypertrophy.short: Growth of a heart chamber where the cavity gets bigger and the wall thickens in proportion. Typical of endurance training, which fills the heart with large volumes for hours.

concentric-hypertrophy.short: Growth of the heart wall inwards, so the wall gets thicker without a bigger cavity. Linked to high pressure loads, such as high blood pressure.

athletes-heart.short: The normal, healthy enlargement of the heart in people who train hard for years: bigger chambers, a bit thicker walls, a slow resting heart rate.

lv-mass.short: The weight of the muscle wall of the left ventricle, in grams, worked out from heart images. It rises with training.

echocardiography.short: An ultrasound scan of the heart: quick and cheap, it shows chamber sizes, wall thickness and how the heart moves.

cardiac-mri.short: A magnetic resonance scan of the heart. Slower and dearer than ultrasound, but it measures chamber volumes and mass more exactly.

angiogenesis.short: The growth of new capillaries from existing ones. Endurance training triggers it in working muscle.

vegf.short: Vascular endothelial growth factor: a signal protein released in muscle that tells capillaries to sprout new branches.

shear-stress.short: The rubbing force of flowing blood on the inner wall of a vessel. More flow means more shear.

endothelium.short: The single layer of cells lining the inside of every blood vessel. It senses blood flow and releases signals that widen or narrow the vessel.

nitric-oxide.short: A small gas molecule made by the endothelium when blood flow rises. It relaxes the vessel's muscle, so the vessel widens.

flow-mediated-dilation.short: A test of artery function: an artery is scanned by ultrasound before and after a cuff is released; the % it widens with the rush of blood shows how well its endothelium works.

red-cell-volume.short: The total volume of red blood cells in the body, in litres. Together with plasma volume it makes up blood volume.

homeostasis.short: The body keeping its inside conditions (temperature, pH, ATP, blood glucose) steady. Exercise disturbs it; the body works to restore it.

hormesis.short: A dose–response where a small or moderate dose of a stress makes the body stronger, while a large dose harms it.
